items.title: Will GM’s 20-Year SAIC China EV Pact Reshape General Motors' (GM) Global Technology Narrative?
items.summary: General Motors and SAIC Motor have extended their SAIC-GM joint venture in China by 20 years to 2047, committing to launch at least 30 new energy vehicles by 2030 and to use China-developed technologies for both domestic and overseas markets. This shift from one-way technology transfer to “local innovation and global sharing” positions GM to tap China’s electric vehicle supply chain and engineering base as a key pillar of its worldwide product and technology roadmap. items.title: General Motors Sets Up $4.5 Billion Safety Net to Avoid Parts Shortages
items.summary: General Motors  stung in recent years by critical parts shortages, is setting up a $4.5 billion safety net designed to keep critical components flowing through supply-chain troubles.  The automaker aims to avoid future parts crunches by securing supplies of high-risk components through a financing arrangement where it pre-funds the purchase of essential parts.  The move, which GM disclosed Tuesday in a regulatory filing, aims to give suppliers enough capital to maintain production and potentially stockpile parts.

items.title: General Motors Dumps Another Major EV Battery Stake; GM Stock Rises
items.summary: General Motors will sell its stake in an Indiana EV battery plant to South Korea's Samsung SDI amid sluggish demand for electric cars. GM stock offered a trendline entry on Tuesday. Ford stock and Tesla stock also gained below key levels.
